title: Prohibit capability claims in configuration entirely
context: rules/common/agents.md:17 and agents/delivery-lead.md:91 both asserted that a child agent does not survive its parent's turn ending and that no way exists to wait, end a turn and be resumed, adding "That is a harness property. Do not try to work around it." Both halves are false. A live experiment ran a parent that dispatched one child and stopped immediately: the parent's last record was 18:09:21 and the child ran to completion at 18:11:27, 124 seconds later, and its result was delivered upward automatically. The harness contradicted the claim in the text of all 55 dispatch results in the incident and lost, because configuration is framed as law and tool output as data.
options: Correct the sentence to state what is true today
Keep capability claims but add a periodic review cadence to re-check them
Prohibit configuration from describing Claude Code's own capabilities at all
outcome: Prohibited, as a standing clause in CLAUDE.md. A capability claim is a cached fact about a system that updates independently, with no expiry mechanism and no way for an agent to falsify it from inside — which makes it self-sealing. Correcting the sentence was rejected because the next harness update makes it false again with nothing to catch it, and a review cadence is itself advisory. Configuration now states preferences, constraints, and facts about this project that the harness cannot know; the harness describes itself at runtime, accurately, for free. Acceptance check 8.4 greps for the claim shapes and must return zero.
